title: Nigerian Chicken Pepper Soup with Red Pepper Broth
summary: A lighter, faster pepper soup: chicken legs cooked in a blended red pepper, onion, ginger and Scotch bonnet base with warm pepper-soup spices, finished with basil.

ingredients.item: red pepper, deseeded and roughly chopped
Scotch bonnet chilli, deseeded for less heat
chicken drumsticks and bone-in thighs, skin removed
fine sea salt or table salt

steps.title: Blend the pepper base
steps.text: Blend the red pepper, onion, Scotch bonnet, ginger and garlic with 100 ml of the water to a smooth orange purée.

steps.title: Coat the chicken
steps.text: Put the chicken in the pot with the purée, all the spice mix (or 1.5 tbsp ready-made Nigerian pepper-soup spice) and half the salt. Stir to coat and leave 10 min.

steps.title: Cook down
steps.text: Cover and cook over medium heat for 10 min, stirring now and then, until the purée darkens a little and the chicken has firmed up.

steps.title: Simmer
steps.text: Add the rest of the water, bring to the boil, then simmer partly covered for 30-35 min until the chicken is tender and reaches 75 °C next to the bone.

steps.title: Season
steps.text: Add the rest of the salt and taste. The broth should be peppery and warming; simmer a few minutes more to concentrate it if you like.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Turn off the heat, stir in the basil and serve in deep bowls, with boiled plantain or rice on the side.

tips: Deseed the Scotch bonnet for a gentler soup, or leave the seeds in for the classic heat.
Skinless chicken keeps the broth clear and less greasy.
A squeeze of lime at the table brightens it.
storage: Keep in the fridge for up to 3 days or freeze for up to 3 months. Reheat until boiling. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
